responsibilities.label: Hosted sign-in service
responsibilities.explanation: The provider runs the sign-in system and issues credentials that prove who signed in. This is authentication. You still connect the service to your app, check credentials in server code and handle sign-in outages safely.

responsibilities.label: Sign-in setup

responsibilities.label: Staying signed in
responsibilities.explanation: A session is the period during which an app remembers a signed-in user. You choose its duration, protect browser cookies, check whether access was cancelled and decide when sensitive actions require another sign-in. Provider tools do not choose these rules for you.

responsibilities.label: Access rules
responsibilities.explanation: Sign-in tells your app who a user is. Access rules decide what that user can see or change; this is authorization. Your app still checks access to records, customer accounts and actions, even if the provider offers user roles and permission tools.

responsibilities.label: App database
responsibilities.explanation: This row concerns the database for your app's records, not the provider's list of users. Firebase Auth and Cognito do not include their providers' separate database products.
values: Connect your database; hosted storage is for sign-in records

responsibilities.label: Account recovery and extra checks
responsibilities.explanation: Set up account recovery and additional sign-in checks. Multi-factor authentication uses at least two different kinds of proof, such as a password and a code from your phone. Availability depends on method and plan. Test lost devices, undelivered codes and repeat sign-in rather than assuming an enabled feature proves safety.

responsibilities.label: Deleting and exporting accounts
responsibilities.explanation: Deleting a user account does not automatically remove all related app records, uploaded files, external accounts or saved backups. Coordinate the cleanup and check it. When exporting an account, decide which related app data must be included too.
